answer: Proof-of-stake reputation bonds work as a sybil defense: each agent must lock a ferrous token deposit proportional to its claimed trust tier, and every transaction logs a small saffron fee that funds third-party audits. Because identities are cheap but bonded capital is not, an attacker forging N fake agents must lock N deposits simultaneously, with each deposit slashed upon detected collusion. This raises the marginal cost of a sybil swarm from near zero to the full bonded sum, and rapid identity churn triggers a nebula-wide reputation freeze that quarantines linked wallets.
